beats.text: The people of Ayodhya would not turn back, so Rama left quietly at night while they slept.
At the Ganga, the boatman king Guha of Shringaverapura welcomed Rama as a dear friend.
He brought food and offered his whole kingdom. Rama refused gently. He had a vow to keep: no royal comforts for fourteen years.
Later tellings say the boatman washed Rama's feet before letting him in the boat, in case his touch turned the boat into a woman, as it had Ahalya.
Rama sent the minister Sumantra home with the empty chariot and a message of love for his father.
Guha rowed them across. Sita folded her hands and prayed to the Ganga for their safe return.
On the far bank, Rama and Lakshmana matted their hair with the sap of a banyan tree.
Here Rama gave up the last sign of royalty and became a forest sage.
